raw_response:
I will not start from zero. I will do almost what I did last year, then adjust a little by cost and by what I saw around me in Quzhou. I have 16.1 mu and only 2 people at home, so I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to hold yield. Cotton can still make money, but it needs more watching and more spraying, so I will not put too much land into it. I will leave 12.0 mu in wheat followed by summer maize, and I will keep 4.1 mu for cotton. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage on wheat jointing and filling, and on maize at the key water times. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than let the crop go hungry, but I still count the money, so I will stay near the rates that worked for me before: wheat a little heavier on nitrogen for tillers and grain, maize enough nitrogen for ear size, and cotton with more potassium because if potassium is short, bolls and fiber are weaker. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it pays clearly, because now most neighbors who get good yield are using those, not old saved seed. For tillage, I will plough the cotton ground, rotary the wheat ground after the previous crop, and mostly no-till the summer maize after wheat harvest so I can save time and catch soil moisture. If weather is normal and I manage water on time, I will aim for steady yield, not gamble on extreme output.
